text:
Bo Horvat is carrying a bigger load for the Islanders. His ice time is up 2.46 minutes a game over his last 10, to about 22 a night, and his individual expected goals (the quality of his own chances) sit at 1.35 per 60 minutes, up from 1.02 last season. That's a top-line center's shot profile.

The points haven't followed all the way: 16 in 16 games, and 9 in the last 10 when our numbers expected about 11. There's no big luck story either way. He has 7 goals on 7.6 expected, and his shooting percentage sits right in his normal range. Horvat is roughly who he's always been, with more chances, and our range has him at 38 goals over the full season (29 to 47).

The rush is his game. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 59% of his shots coming off the rush last season, and he does it against the other team's best (Evolving-Hockey put his competition in the 99th percentile). His linemates may shift soon, with Islanders reporter Stefen Rosner asking where Mathew Barzal fits and whether Matias Maccelli reunites with Horvat. The shot volume says he'll be fine either way.
headline: Horvat's chances are up even if the points lag
